record.hypothesis: Across all four categories, add a recency input feature: scale visible item vectors by 1+0.10*r, where r runs linearly from -1 to 1 over visible chronological ranks (singleton r=0); padding stays zero and mask scale stays one. Jointly set dropout=0.1 and LR=7e-4, retaining width 64 and length 128. Recency emphasizes recent context, while reduced dropout preserves that small signal and lower LR moderates fitting. Keep loss, embedding parameterization and backbone unchanged. Retain one BERT4Rec checkpoint/category, seed 42, 200 batches/epoch and the 200-epoch cap; mirror features in the predictor writer.

             seq, self.effective_item_weight(), padding_idx=0
         )
+        visible = (seq > 0) & (seq <= self.itemnum)
+        visible_rank = visible.long().cumsum(dim=1).to(item_vectors.dtype)
+        visible_count = visible.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).to(item_vectors.dtype)
+        recency = 2.0 * (visible_rank - 1.0) / (visible_count - 1.0).clamp_min(1.0) - 1.0
+        recency = torch.where(
+            visible & (visible_count > 1.0), recency, torch.zeros_like(recency)
+        )
+        item_vectors = item_vectors * (1.0 + 0.10 * recency).unsqueeze(-1)
         x = item_vectors * (self.hidden_units ** 0.5) + self.pos_emb(pos)
         x = self.dropout(x)

category_rationales.rationale: Across all four categories, jointly reduce dropout to 0.1 and learning rate to 7e-4. Reduced dropout preserves the small recency signal, while smaller updates moderate fitting. Retain width 64, history length 128 and the existing training limits.

Scale visible item vectors by 1+0.10*r using chronological ranks among visible real items only. Multiple visible items span r=-1 to 1; singleton histories use r=0. Padding remains zero and mask tokens retain scale one. The generated predictor imports this same model class, so training and appended-mask inference share the feature without checkpoint shape changes.
